rationale: Evidence from iteration 4 (score 709.6, best so far): the oval (953) and s-bend (944) both finish 20/20, with s-bend control effort and oscillation acceptable. The slalom is the whole gap. It finishes 0/20 (off-track 18, timeout 2), with progress 0.55, about 0.9 line-loss events per run and max_error 0.0595, right at the 0.06 m off-track limit. Score is the mean of the three tracks, so a finished slalom would add roughly 500 to 700 points on that track. Iteration 2 to 4 showed that a larger sensor footprint (0.012 to 0.016) plus more derivative damping (kd 0.8 to 1.0) roughly doubled slalom progress without hurting the other tracks. Derivative damping and the footprint are therefore still the productive levers. Two changes this iteration: (1) kd 1.0 to 1.3 for more damping against the quick left-right signal swings of the slalom. (2) wheel_track 0.12 to 0.11. Turn rate is the wheel speed difference divided by track, and the controller's differential is fixed at 350 PWM per unit of turn, so a narrower track gives about 9% more yaw response per unit of kp. This helps the slalom's tight alternating bends, where the robot currently falls behind the tape. Sensor array (x = -0.04 to +0.04, 0.02 spacing, 0.016 size), kp 2.0, ki 0, base_speed 1.0, last_direction line loss and the other geometry are unchanged, so the oval and s-bend behaviour should stay close to iteration 4. Expected result: slalom line losses fall below 0.5 per run and progress rises above 0.6, with a chance of finishing some slalom runs. Oval and s-bend should hold near 1.0 finish. Hypotheses: H1, the slalom off-track exits come from insufficient yaw response at tight alternations, which the narrower track addresses. H2, the extra kd reduces overshoot, so max_error on the slalom drops below 0.05. Risk: the combined response increase could bring back s-bend oscillation (control effort was 4.3 at iteration 4). Next measurements: per-track max_error, line_loss_events and progress, and slalom completion_time to see whether the robot can meet the 3 s limit at base_speed 1.0. If the s-bend control effort rises above 6, I will back off the wheel_track change first.
